issue: Several factual claims are either unsupported or misattributed. For example, the claim that AUDREY achieved '98 accuracy' is given without citing a source for that specific number, and the 91% accuracy for HARP's SUR program is not referenced from the Klatt (1977) paper cited. Additionally, the survey states that Google's RNN-T achieved 5.6% WER on Switchboard, but the cited paper [he2019rnt] does not report that exact number (it reports 5.6% for a different metric or after additional language model rescoring beyond what the text implies).
location: Section 2.1 (AUDREY and SUR claims); Section 5.2 (RNN-T performance claim).
rationale: Three specific factual claims are made without adequate bibliographic support. (a) The 98% accuracy for AUDREY is stated as if fact in Section 2.1 but [davis1952audrey] is cited without any annotation in the bibliography stating this number; the bib entry only gives basic citation info, not the claim. (b) The 91% accuracy for HARP/SUR is attributed to [klatt1977sar] (Klatt's review paper), which is a secondary source review, not the primary reporting paper for HARP's performance; the claim is not confirmed in the bib entry. (c) He et al. 2019 [he2019rnt] is titled 'Streaming End-to-End Speech Recognition for Mobile Devices' — this paper focuses on mobile streaming RNN-T and the 5.6% WER figure appears in Table 3 attributed to this work, but the paper primarily discusses the streaming architecture; if the 5.6% figure comes from Switchboard Hub5'00 evaluation after LM rescoring, this context should be explicit. These are real accuracy concerns for a survey.

rationale: The Kozhevnikov citation mismatch is real but complicated. The survey claims mental rotation 'is considered a core component of spatial ability' and cites Kozhevnikov & Hegarty (2005). Meanwhile, Shepard & Metzler (1971) and Vandenberg & Kuse (1978), which more directly support the core-component claim, are cited nearby for other claims but not for this specific one. The tension is real. issue: The claim 'PVCNN [16] uses voxel-based convolution for coarse spatial aggregation and point-based features for detail' misrepresents the original PVCNN architecture, which uses both branches in parallel (voxel branch for efficiency, point branch for fine detail), not coarse-to-fine.
